observations.text: The header says the import validates data integrity using checksums, but 3000-VALIDATE-IMPORT only displays 'Import validation completed' and 'No validation errors detected' without performing any check.

EXPORT-INPUT is declared INDEXED with RECORD KEY EXPORT-SEQUENCE-NUM, which is defined in WORKING-STORAGE (COPY CVEXPORT) rather than in the FD record EXPORT-INPUT-RECORD; the same defect exists in CBEXPORT.
A failed write to the error file only displays a message; processing continues and WS-ERROR-RECORDS-WRITTEN is still incremented.

ERR-SEQUENCE is PIC 9(07) while EXPORT-SEQUENCE-NUM is PIC 9(9), so sequence numbers above 9,999,999 are truncated in error records; ERR-TIMESTAMP receives the raw 21-character FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE rather than a formatted timestamp.
The header lists four target files (CUSTOMER, ACCOUNT, CARD-XREF, TRANSACTION), but the program also writes a fifth, CARD-OUTPUT (CARDOUT).
4000-FINALIZE closes all files without checking their status.

paragraphs.logic: Performs 1000-INITIALIZE, 2000-PROCESS-EXPORT-FILE, 3000-VALIDATE-IMPORT (a stub) and 4000-FINALIZE, and ends with GOBACK.
paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN-PROCESSING

paragraphs.logic: Displays a start message, formats WS-IMPORT-DATE (YYYY-MM-DD) and WS-IMPORT-TIME (HH:MM:SS) from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE, opens all files and displays the import date and time.
paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE

paragraphs.logic: Opens EXPORT-INPUT for INPUT and CUSTOMER-OUTPUT, ACCOUNT-OUTPUT, XREF-OUTPUT, TRANSACTION-OUTPUT, CARD-OUTPUT and ERROR-OUTPUT for OUTPUT. After each OPEN, when its status condition (for example WS-EXPORT-OK, WS-CUSTOMER-OK, WS-ERROR-OK) is false it displays 'ERROR: Cannot open <file>, Status: ' with the status field and performs 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM.
paragraphs.name: 1100-OPEN-FILES

paragraphs.logic: Reads export records until WS-EXPORT-EOF, counting each in WS-TOTAL-RECORDS-READ and dispatching it by record type.
paragraphs.name: 2000-PROCESS-EXPORT-FILE

paragraphs.logic: Reads the next EXPORT-INPUT record into EXPORT-RECORD; a status other than '00' or '10' displays 'ERROR: Reading EXPORT-INPUT, Status: ' and abends.
paragraphs.name: 2100-READ-EXPORT-RECORD

paragraphs.logic: EVALUATEs EXPORT-REC-TYPE: 'C' customer, 'A' account, 'X' cross-reference, 'T' transaction, 'D' card; any other value goes to 2700-PROCESS-UNKNOWN-RECORD.
paragraphs.name: 2200-PROCESS-RECORD-BY-TYPE

paragraphs.logic: Initializes CUSTOMER-RECORD, moves every EXP-CUST-* field (array elements to address lines 1-3 and phones 1-2) into it, writes it to CUSTOUT (abend on status not '00') and increments the customer counter.
paragraphs.name: 2300-PROCESS-CUSTOMER-RECORD

paragraphs.logic: Initializes ACCOUNT-RECORD, moves every EXP-ACCT-* field into it (unpacking COMP/COMP-3 to display), writes it to ACCTOUT (abend on status not '00') and increments the account counter.
paragraphs.name: 2400-PROCESS-ACCOUNT-RECORD

paragraphs.logic: Initializes CARD-XREF-RECORD, moves card number, customer id and account id, writes it to XREFOUT (abend on status not '00') and increments the xref counter.
paragraphs.name: 2500-PROCESS-XREF-RECORD

paragraphs.logic: Initializes TRAN-RECORD, moves every EXP-TRAN-* field into it, writes it to TRNXOUT (abend on status not '00') and increments the transaction counter.
paragraphs.name: 2600-PROCESS-TRAN-RECORD

paragraphs.logic: Initializes CARD-RECORD, moves card number, account id, CVV, embossed name, expiration date and active status, writes it to CARDOUT (abend on status not '00') and increments the card counter.
paragraphs.name: 2650-PROCESS-CARD-RECORD

paragraphs.logic: Increments WS-UNKNOWN-RECORD-TYPE-COUNT, fills WS-ERROR-RECORD with current date/time, the record type, the export sequence number and 'Unknown record type encountered', and writes it via 2750-WRITE-ERROR.
paragraphs.name: 2700-PROCESS-UNKNOWN-RECORD

paragraphs.logic: Writes WS-ERROR-RECORD to ERROUT; on a bad status only displays 'ERROR: Writing error record, Status: '. Always increments WS-ERROR-RECORDS-WRITTEN.
paragraphs.name: 2750-WRITE-ERROR

paragraphs.logic: Placeholder: displays 'CBIMPORT: Import validation completed' and 'CBIMPORT: No validation errors detected' without any checks.
paragraphs.name: 3000-VALIDATE-IMPORT

paragraphs.logic: Closes EXPORT-INPUT and the six output files (statuses not checked), displays 'CBIMPORT: Import completed' and the counters WS-TOTAL-RECORDS-READ, WS-CUSTOMER-RECORDS-IMPORTED, WS-ACCOUNT-RECORDS-IMPORTED, WS-XREF-RECORDS-IMPORTED, WS-TRAN-RECORDS-IMPORTED, WS-CARD-RECORDS-IMPORTED, WS-ERROR-RECORDS-WRITTEN and WS-UNKNOWN-RECORD-TYPE-COUNT.
paragraphs.name: 4000-FINALIZE

paragraphs.logic: Displays 'CBIMPORT: ABENDING PROGRAM' and calls CEE3ABD without parameters.
paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM

rules.outcome: Record written to CUSTOUT, ACCTOUT, XREFOUT, TRNXOUT or CARDOUT, or handled by 2700-PROCESS-UNKNOWN-RECORD.
rules.statement: Each export record is routed to its normalized target file by EXPORT-REC-TYPE: 'C' to the customer file, 'A' to the account file, 'X' to the card cross-reference file, 'T' to the transaction file, 'D' to the card file; any other type is treated as an unknown record.

rules.anchor: MOVE 'Unknown record type encountered' TO ERR-MESSAGE
rules.outcome: Error record written to ERROUT; WS-UNKNOWN-RECORD-TYPE-COUNT and WS-ERROR-RECORDS-WRITTEN incremented.
rules.statement: A record with an unknown type is not imported and does not stop the run: it is counted, logged to the error file with timestamp, type, sequence number and 'Unknown record type encountered', and processing continues.

rules.conditions: Open status not '00'; read status not '00'/'10'; write status not '00'.
rules.outcome: Abend; target files may be partially written.
rules.statement: Failure to open any file, a read error on the export file (status not '00'/'10'), or a failed write to any target master file aborts the import via CEE3ABD.

rules.outcome: One record written to the matching target file.
rules.statement: Imported records are rebuilt field by field into the standard CardDemo master layouts (customer 500, account 300, cross-reference 50, transaction 350, card 150 bytes), converting the export's packed (COMP/COMP-3) numeric fields back to the display formats of CVCUS01Y, CVACT01Y, CVACT03Y, CVTRA05Y and CVACT02Y. No field is validated or altered.

sme_questions.question: What checksum or integrity validation is 3000-VALIDATE-IMPORT supposed to perform (the header promises checksums)?
Should a write failure on the error file abend the run, as failures on the master target files do?

summary.text: CBIMPORT is the batch counterpart of CBEXPORT for branch migration. It reads the 500-byte multi-record export file EXPFILE (layout CVEXPORT) and splits it by record type into sequential customer (CUSTOUT), account (ACCTOUT), card cross-reference (XREFOUT), transaction (TRNXOUT) and card (CARDOUT) files in the standard CardDemo layouts, unpacking COMP/COMP-3 fields. Records with an unknown type are logged to the 132-byte error file ERROUT and skipped. The validation step is a stub that always reports no errors. It ends by displaying read, import, error and unknown-type counts; open, read and master-file write errors abend the run via CEE3ABD.
